trivia: Germany's high figure reflects near-universal completion of dual-track vocational Sekundarstufe II programs, which count as upper-secondary schooling in the UN calculation.

title: Highest English proficiency (non-native)
prompt: Name the countries with the highest EF English Proficiency Index score among nations where English is not the primary native language.

source.name: EF Education First — English Proficiency Index (EF EPI)

disclaimer: EF EPI ranks non-native-English countries by test-taker scores. Native-English-speaking countries (US, UK, Ireland, Australia, etc.) are excluded from the index by design.
trivia: The Nordic countries have held the top of the EF EPI every year since the index launched in 2011 — Sweden topped the very first edition in 2011 with 66.8.

title: Most doctorates awarded per year
prompt: Name the countries that award the most doctoral (PhD-level) degrees annually.

source.name: OECD Education at a Glance / UNESCO Institute for Statistics — Doctoral Graduates (ISCED 8)

disclaimer: Total number of ISCED-8 (doctoral) degrees awarded in a single reporting year. China's figure is from national Ministry of Education statistics; other countries from OECD / UIS returns.
trivia: The US has awarded more STEM PhDs than any other country every year since 1958, though China surpassed it in total doctoral awards around 2018.

title: Highest spending per student (secondary)
prompt: Name the countries that spend the most per secondary-school student on education.

source.name: OECD — Education at a Glance 2024, Expenditure per Student (Secondary)

disclaimer: Annual expenditure per full-time equivalent student in secondary education, USD equivalent using PPP. Includes both public and private funding.
trivia: Luxembourg spends more per student than any other OECD country at every level — a function of both wealth and very small class sizes in a country with fewer than 700,000 residents.

title: Most students studying abroad
prompt: Name the countries whose citizens make up the largest populations of internationally mobile tertiary students studying abroad.

source.name: UNESCO Institute for Statistics — Global Flow of Tertiary-Level Students

disclaimer: Counts students of a given nationality enrolled in higher education outside their country of origin. Includes all ISCED-5-through-8 tertiary programs.
trivia: Chinese students abroad outnumber Indian students abroad by roughly 2 to 1, and together the two countries send more students overseas than the next ten sending countries combined.

title: Lowest secondary student-teacher ratio
prompt: Name the countries with the smallest number of students per teacher in secondary education.

source.name: World Bank / UNESCO UIS — Pupil-Teacher Ratio, Secondary

disclaimer: Ratio of enrolled secondary students to full-time-equivalent teachers. Lower is more favorable. Micro-states with fewer than 100,000 residents are excluded so comparisons stay meaningful.
trivia: San Marino and Liechtenstein report even lower ratios but are excluded here as microstates; among larger countries Portugal has held the top position for over a decade.

title: Highest adult numeracy (PIAAC)
prompt: Name the countries whose adults scored highest on the OECD PIAAC adult numeracy assessment.

source.name: OECD — Survey of Adult Skills (PIAAC), Cycle 2

disclaimer: PIAAC numeracy scale centered at 250. Ranked by mean score of adults aged 16-65. Only countries participating in Cycle 2 (2023) are ranked here.
trivia: Japan tops both PIAAC numeracy and PIAAC literacy — the only country to lead both scales in Cycle 2.

title: Most Fields Medals awarded
prompt: Name the countries whose mathematicians have won the most Fields Medals since the prize was first awarded in 1936.

source.name: International Mathematical Union — Fields Medal Laureates

disclaimer: Attributed to the primary country of the mathematician at the time of the award, per the IMU citation. Dual-national laureates count for both listed countries. Soviet-era laureates are counted under Russia with an implicit successor mapping.
trivia: France's outsized total is anchored by the École Normale Supérieure — 12 of France's Fields Medalists studied or taught there at some point in their careers.

title: Largest personal luxury goods markets
prompt: Name the countries with the largest personal luxury goods markets by total retail sales value.

source.name: Bain & Company / Altagamma — Luxury Goods Worldwide Market Study

disclaimer: Total resident + tourist spend on personal luxury goods (apparel, leather, jewelry, watches, beauty). USD, current exchange rates.
trivia: Chinese consumers globally account for roughly a third of all personal luxury goods spending, but only about half of that spend happens inside mainland China — the rest is in Paris, Milan, and Hong Kong.

title: Most Deloitte Top 100 luxury company HQs
prompt: Name the countries that are home to the most companies on Deloitte's Global Powers of Luxury Goods Top 100.

source.name: Deloitte — Global Powers of Luxury Goods

disclaimer: Ranked by number of Top 100 luxury-goods companies headquartered in each country, based on the group's country of registration.
trivia: Italian houses dominate by count but not by revenue — the French Top 100 companies (led by LVMH and Kering) generate roughly half of the entire Top 100's combined sales.

title: Top handbag & leather goods exporters
prompt: Name the countries with the largest exports of handbags, wallets, and leather travel goods by value.

source.name: ITC Trade Map / OEC — HS 4202 (trunks, suitcases, handbags, wallets)

disclaimer: HS chapter 4202 — trunks, suitcases, handbags, wallets, and similar articles. Covers all materials, not leather only.
trivia: France leads by value despite exporting only a fraction of China's unit volume — a single Hermès Birkin can outsell hundreds of Chinese-manufactured handbags on the customs value line.

title: Top perfume & fragrance exporters
prompt: Name the countries with the largest exports of perfumes and toilet waters by value.

source.name: ITC Trade Map / OEC — HS 3303 (perfumes and toilet waters)

disclaimer: HS 3303 — perfumes and toilet waters. Excludes essential oils (HS 3301) and other cosmetics/toiletries.
trivia: France's fragrance exports are anchored by a handful of legacy houses — Chanel No.5 alone reportedly sells a bottle every 30 seconds worldwide.

title: Top rough diamond exporters
prompt: Name the countries with the largest exports of rough (uncut) diamonds by value.

source.name: Kimberley Process Certification Scheme — Annual Global Summary

disclaimer: Rough (uncut) diamond exports by value under the Kimberley Process. Excludes polished / cut diamonds (India dominates that trade).
trivia: Botswana's Jwaneng mine alone is the single most valuable diamond mine in the world by output, and diamonds account for roughly 80% of the country's exports.

title: Top jewelry exporters
prompt: Name the countries with the largest exports of jewelry articles by value.

source.name: ITC Trade Map / OEC — HS 7113 (articles of jewelry of precious metal)

disclaimer: HS 7113 — jewelry articles of precious metal. Includes gold and silver jewelry; excludes loose gems and pearls.
trivia: India is the world's largest jewelry manufacturing hub by workforce — the industry employs an estimated 4-5 million people, most concentrated in Mumbai and Surat.

title: Largest gold jewelry consumers
prompt: Name the countries that consume the most gold jewelry annually by weight.

source.name: World Gold Council — Gold Demand Trends

disclaimer: Consumer gold jewelry demand in tonnes. Retail purchases of finished jewelry only — excludes central-bank buying and investment bars/coins.
trivia: Together, India and China account for roughly half of world gold jewelry demand — Diwali and Chinese New Year alone visibly move the global gold price.

title: Top footwear exporters
prompt: Name the countries with the largest exports of footwear by value.

source.name: World Footwear Yearbook / ITC Trade Map — HS 64

disclaimer: HS chapter 64 — all footwear categories (leather, athletic, plastic/rubber). Ranked by export value in USD.
trivia: Vietnam has quietly overtaken every other country except China in athletic footwear specifically — Nike alone produces roughly half of its shoes there.

title: Top raw cotton exporters
prompt: Name the countries with the largest exports of raw cotton by value.

source.name: ITC Trade Map / OEC — HS 5201 (cotton, not carded or combed)

disclaimer: HS 5201 — raw (unprocessed) cotton fiber. Excludes cotton yarn, fabric, and finished cotton apparel.
trivia: The US, Brazil, and Australia together supply the majority of world raw cotton exports even though China and India grow more cotton overall — those two consume most of their own production domestically.

title: Top leather exporters
prompt: Name the countries with the largest exports of tanned leather and hides by value.

source.name: ITC Trade Map / OEC — HS 41 (raw hides, skins, and leather)

disclaimer: HS chapter 41 — raw hides, skins, and tanned leather. Excludes finished leather goods (handbags, shoes, garments).
trivia: Italy alone processes roughly a fifth of the world's finished tanned leather — the Arzignano and Santa Croce sull'Arno tanning districts have been leather-tanning centers since the Middle Ages.

title: Largest athletic footwear markets
prompt: Name the countries with the largest athletic footwear (sneakers) markets by retail sales value.

source.name: Statista — Athletic Footwear market outlook

disclaimer: Retail sales of athletic and sports footwear (sneakers, running, basketball, training). USD, current exchange rates.
trivia: US sneaker resale alone is estimated at $2B annually — StockX and GOAT both report the US as by far their largest customer base for secondary-market Jordans and Yeezys.

title: Top textile yarn exporters
prompt: Name the countries with the largest exports of textile yarn (natural and synthetic) by value.

source.name: ITC Trade Map / OEC — HS 52-55 yarns (cotton, wool, and man-made fiber yarns)

disclaimer: Combined textile yarn exports across HS 5205-5207 (cotton), HS 5106-5110 (wool), and HS 5402/5509 (man-made fiber yarns).
trivia: Vietnam has climbed the yarn export rankings faster than any other country in the last decade, driven almost entirely by demand from its own downstream garment industry.

title: Highest Age at First Marriage (Men)
prompt: Name the countries where men marry latest, ranked by mean age at first marriage for men.

source.name: UN DESA — World Marriage Data 2019
source.asOf: UN WMD 2019 (latest available observation per country)

disclaimer: Mean (or singulate mean) age at first marriage for men, using each country's most recent census or vital-statistics observation. Cohabitation is not counted as marriage.
trivia: Nordic and Southern European countries dominate the top of this ranking because delayed household formation is now the norm across Europe — but the pattern started earliest in Sweden and Denmark in the 1970s.
asOfDate: UN WMD 2019 (latest available observation per country)

title: Lowest Divorce Rate
prompt: Name the countries with the lowest crude divorce rate (divorces per 1,000 people per year).

source.name: UN Demographic Yearbook — Marriage and Divorce Statistics

disclaimer: Crude divorce rate = judicial dissolutions per 1,000 mid-year population. Excludes religious annulments and informal separations, so countries where civil divorce is rare or restricted rank low here regardless of union stability.
trivia: Divorce was not legalized in the Philippines at all as of the source year (it remains one of only two states in the world, alongside Vatican City, without a general civil divorce law).

title: Highest Mean Age at First Childbirth
prompt: Name the countries where women have their first child latest, ranked by mean age at first birth.

source.name: OECD Family Database — SF2.3 Mean age at first childbirth

disclaimer: Mean age of mother at first live birth. Uses each country's most recent vital-statistics report. Excludes stillbirths.
trivia: In every OECD country the mean age at first birth has risen by more than three years since 1980; South Korea's rose fastest, by more than five years.

title: Highest Marriage Rate
prompt: Name the countries with the highest crude marriage rate (marriages per 1,000 people per year).

source.name: UN Demographic Yearbook — Marriages and Crude Marriage Rates

disclaimer: Crude marriage rate = registered marriages per 1,000 mid-year population. Includes destination-marriage jurisdictions where the marriage is registered but at least one spouse is non-resident.
trivia: Cyprus and Seychelles rank high partly because they are popular destination-wedding jurisdictions — a significant share of marriages registered there involve non-resident couples.

title: Highest Out-of-Wedlock Birth Share
prompt: Name the countries with the highest share of births to unmarried mothers.

source.name: OECD Family Database — SF2.4 Share of births outside of marriage

disclaimer: Percent of live births where the registered mother was not married at the time of the birth. Includes births to cohabiting parents, which drives most of the number in Europe and Latin America.
trivia: In Iceland and Chile more than 70% of first children are born to unmarried parents — but the vast majority are born to stable cohabiting couples, not single mothers.

title: Highest Single-Parent Household Share
prompt: Name the countries with the highest share of children living in single-parent households.

source.name: Pew Research Center — Children living with a single parent (global)

disclaimer: Share of children under 18 living with only one parent (biological, step, or adoptive) and no other adult. Based on the most recent nationally representative household survey for each country.
trivia: The United States has by far the highest single-parent share of any wealthy country — nearly a quarter of American children live with a single parent, roughly three times the rate in Japan or Turkey.

title: Best UN Gender Inequality Index (Lowest GII)
prompt: Name the countries with the lowest score on the UN Gender Inequality Index (the most gender-equal countries).

source.name: UNDP Human Development Report — Gender Inequality Index (GII)

disclaimer: Composite index (0 = perfect equality, 1 = maximum inequality) built from reproductive health, empowerment (parliament seats + secondary education) and labour market participation. Lower is better. Rank 1 is the most equal country.
trivia: The GII combines three domains, so a country can top it by excelling in maternal mortality and parliamentary representation even without leading on labour-force participation — which is why Denmark and Norway outrank Iceland in GII despite Iceland's WEF Gender Gap Index #1 position.

title: Highest Femicide Rate
prompt: Name the countries with the highest femicide rate (intentional homicides of women and girls by intimate partners or family members, per 100,000 female population).

source.name: UNODC / UN Women — Gender-related killings of women and girls

disclaimer: Rate of intentional female homicides attributable to intimate partners or other family members, per 100,000 females. Only countries reporting disaggregated data to UNODC are included; several high-incidence countries do not report.
trivia: UNODC estimates that more than 55% of female homicide victims worldwide are killed by their partners or relatives, compared with under 12% for male homicide victims.

title: Best Women's Economic Participation Score (WEF)
prompt: Name the countries with the highest score on the WEF Global Gender Gap Report's Economic Participation and Opportunity subindex.

source.name: World Economic Forum — Global Gender Gap Report 2023

disclaimer: The Economic Participation and Opportunity subindex (0 = maximum gap, 1 = parity) combines female-to-male ratios on labour-force participation, wage equality for similar work, estimated earned income, and share of legislators/senior officials/managers. Higher is better.
trivia: This subindex is the hardest of the four WEF subindices to close — no country has ever reached parity on it, while Health and Educational Attainment have been at or above 95% globally for over a decade.

title: Best Women's Political Empowerment Score (WEF)
prompt: Name the countries with the highest score on the WEF Global Gender Gap Report's Political Empowerment subindex.

source.name: World Economic Forum — Global Gender Gap Report 2023

disclaimer: The Political Empowerment subindex (0 = maximum gap, 1 = parity) combines female-to-male ratios for parliamentary seats, ministerial positions, and years with a female head of state over the last 50 years. Higher is better.
trivia: This is the widest of the four WEF gender-gap subindices — the global average score is under 0.25, meaning the world has closed less than a quarter of the political-empowerment gap.

title: Highest Female Tertiary Enrolment vs Men
prompt: Name the countries where women out-enrol men in tertiary (post-secondary) education by the widest margin, ranked by female-to-male gross tertiary enrolment ratio.

source.name: UNESCO Institute for Statistics — Gender parity index for tertiary GER

disclaimer: Female-to-male ratio of the gross tertiary enrolment ratio (GPI). Values above 1.0 mean more women than men enrol; the ratio can exceed 2.0 in small states where a large share of male school-leavers migrate abroad for work.
trivia: In Qatar, migrant labour patterns mean the domestic tertiary system is overwhelmingly female — the population of male tertiary-age nationals is small and many study abroad, producing the world's most extreme female-skewed enrolment ratio.

title: Lowest Marriage Rate
prompt: Name the countries with the lowest crude marriage rate (marriages per 1,000 people per year).

source.name: UN Demographic Yearbook — Marriages and Crude Marriage Rates

disclaimer: Crude marriage rate = registered marriages per 1,000 mid-year population. 2020 was depressed by pandemic restrictions on ceremonies in many countries, exaggerating the fall in states where cohabitation is already the norm.
trivia: In Portugal, Italy and Argentina the marriage rate has more than halved since 2000 as long-term cohabitation replaced first marriages — but the underlying rate of couple formation has barely changed.

title: Most Time Zones
prompt: Name the countries whose territory (including overseas dependencies) spans the most standard time zones.

source.name: CIA World Factbook — Time zones by country

disclaimer: Counts distinct standard-time offsets across all inhabited territories, including overseas departments and dependencies. Half-hour offsets counted as separate zones.
trivia: France leads because its overseas territories span from French Polynesia (UTC-10) through Reunion (UTC+4) — a wider east-west spread than mainland Russia.

answers.value: 1 zone (Prince Edward Islands share) — commonly listed as 2

title: Most First-Order Subdivisions
prompt: Name the countries with the most first-order administrative subdivisions (states, provinces, oblasts, regions, or equivalents).

source.name: Statoids — Administrative divisions of countries

disclaimer: Counts primary administrative divisions only (states, provinces, regions, oblasts). Excludes autonomous cities where they are secondary to a province structure. Federal districts and capital territories included where treated as first-order.
trivia: Russia's 89 federal subjects include four annexed Ukrainian territories claimed after 2022 that most of the world does not recognise.

title: Longest North-South Extent
prompt: Name the countries with the longest north-south span (greatest distance in kilometres between northernmost and southernmost points of contiguous mainland territory).

source.name: Nations Online — Country geographic extents

disclaimer: Mainland only — excludes overseas territories and dependencies. Measured as great-circle distance between northernmost and southernmost points of contiguous territory.
trivia: Chile stretches more than 4,300 km north to south but is on average only 177 km wide — the world's most elongated country by aspect ratio.

title: Longest East-West Extent
prompt: Name the countries with the longest east-west span (greatest distance in kilometres between easternmost and westernmost land points of contiguous mainland).

source.name: Nations Online — Country geographic extents

disclaimer: Mainland measurements; excludes non-contiguous overseas territories. Great-circle distance between extreme east and west points.
trivia: Russia's east-west span crosses more than 170 degrees of longitude — nearly half the globe — from Kaliningrad on the Baltic to Cape Dezhnev on the Bering Strait.

title: Most Active Volcanoes
prompt: Name the countries with the most Holocene-active volcanoes (having erupted in roughly the last 11,700 years).

source.name: Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program

disclaimer: Counts Holocene-active volcanoes as catalogued by the Smithsonian. Includes both currently erupting and dormant but potentially active systems.
trivia: The United States tops the list thanks to Alaska's Aleutian Arc — but Indonesia has more currently-erupting volcanoes than any other country.

title: Most UNESCO Global Geoparks
prompt: Name the countries with the most UNESCO Global Geoparks — protected sites of international geological significance.

source.name: UNESCO — Global Geoparks Network

disclaimer: UNESCO Global Geoparks are distinct from UNESCO World Heritage Sites. Only sites recognised through the International Geoscience and Geoparks Programme count.
trivia: The UNESCO Global Geoparks label was created in 2015; China's Zhangjiajie geopark — with quartzite sandstone pillars — inspired the floating mountains in the film Avatar.

title: Most Ramsar Wetland Sites
prompt: Name the countries with the most Ramsar-designated wetlands of international importance.

source.name: Ramsar Convention Secretariat

disclaimer: Counts number of designated sites, not total wetland area. Ramsar designation is voluntary and reflects both wetland extent and government participation in the Convention.
trivia: The Ramsar Convention was signed in the Iranian city of Ramsar in 1971 — the first modern international environmental treaty.

title: Countries with Highest Freshwater Withdrawal
prompt: Name the countries with the highest annual total freshwater withdrawal (surface and groundwater combined) in cubic kilometres per year.

source.name: FAO AQUASTAT — Freshwater withdrawal by country

disclaimer: Includes agricultural, industrial and municipal withdrawal. Not the same as freshwater consumption — some withdrawn water is returned to source.
trivia: Agriculture accounts for about 70% of global freshwater withdrawal; irrigation of rice, wheat and cotton alone consumes more water than all households on Earth combined.

title: Longest Great-Circle Diameter
prompt: Name the countries with the greatest great-circle distance between their two farthest-apart points (including all territories and dependencies).

source.name: CIA World Factbook — Geographic coordinates & extents

disclaimer: Great-circle distance between the two most distant points in each country, including inhabited overseas territories and dependencies where applicable. Uninhabited claims (e.g. Antarctic sectors) excluded.
trivia: France's diameter is inflated by its Pacific territories — Tahiti is farther from Paris than New York is from Beijing.

title: Highest Elevation Range
prompt: Name the countries with the greatest elevation range — the vertical distance between their highest and lowest natural land points.

source.name: Peakbagger + national geological surveys

disclaimer: Elevation range = highest point minus lowest natural land point (below sea level counted as negative). Excludes coastal deep-sea trenches; land-based extremes only.
trivia: Nepal has 8 of the world's 14 peaks above 8,000 m but only ranks in the top half here because its lowest point is a modest 59 m above sea level — countries with sub-sea-level basins gain a boost.

title: Highest Terrestrial Protected Area Share
prompt: Name the countries with the highest share of national land area formally protected (national parks, reserves, and other IUCN-recognised categories).

source.name: Protected Planet — World Database on Protected Areas

disclaimer: Percentage of total terrestrial area under formal protection according to IUCN categories I–VI. Marine protected areas excluded. Microstates with total-territory reserves excluded.
trivia: Venezuela's high protected-area share exists mostly on paper — enforcement in the Amazonas region has collapsed since 2015, and illegal gold mining now scars several of its largest national parks.

title: Largest Peatland Area
prompt: Name the countries with the largest total area of peatlands (bogs, mires, fens, and peat swamp forests).

source.name: Global Peatland Assessment — UNEP

disclaimer: Includes all peat-forming wetland types with organic soil layers over 30 cm thick. Estimates carry ±20% uncertainty in tropical countries where mapping remains incomplete.
trivia: Peatlands cover just 3% of Earth's land surface but store twice as much carbon as all the world's forests combined.

title: Largest Permafrost Area
prompt: Name the countries with the largest total land area underlain by permafrost (continuous, discontinuous, or sporadic).

source.name: International Permafrost Association — Circumpolar Permafrost Map

disclaimer: Total area with permafrost at any depth, including sporadic and discontinuous zones. Southern hemisphere permafrost (South American Andes, Antarctica-adjacent islands) is a rounding error compared with Arctic zones.
trivia: Permafrost across the Arctic contains roughly twice the carbon currently in the atmosphere — thawing it is one of the largest climate-tipping risks scientists track.

title: Largest Arable Land Area
prompt: Name the countries with the largest total area of arable land (land under temporary agricultural crops or fallow, per FAO definition).

source.name: FAOSTAT — Land use indicators

disclaimer: Arable land = temporary crops, meadows for mowing, market/kitchen gardens, and fallow land. Excludes permanent crops (orchards, vineyards), permanent pasture, and forest.
trivia: India has the largest arable-land area on Earth despite being only one-third the size of the United States — nearly 60% of its territory is farmed, the highest share of any large country.

title: Largest Boreal Forest Area
prompt: Name the countries with the largest area of boreal (taiga) forest — subarctic coniferous forest between roughly 50°N and 70°N latitude.

source.name: FAO Global Forest Resources Assessment

disclaimer: Boreal forest area defined by FAO ecological zone classification (evergreen and deciduous needle-leaf forests in subarctic climate). Excludes temperate coniferous forest further south.
trivia: The boreal biome forms an unbroken ring of forest around the northern hemisphere — a single biological unit larger than the Amazon rainforest, and the world's largest terrestrial biome.

title: Oldest continuously reigning monarchies
prompt: Name the countries with the oldest continuously reigning monarchies (measured from the earliest date of the current dynasty or unbroken monarchical line).

source.name: Britannica / royal-house historical records (aggregated)

disclaimer: Measured from the traditional founding date of the current dynasty or unbroken monarchical succession; interregnums such as republics or foreign occupations that were later restored to the same dynasty are noted where they interrupt continuity. Ties broken alphabetically.
trivia: Japan's Imperial House traces its succession to Emperor Jimmu in 660 BCE, though the earliest historically verifiable emperors date to the 6th century CE.

title: Oldest currencies still in circulation
prompt: Name the countries whose currently circulating national currency has the oldest continuous use under its current name.

source.name: Central bank histories / Britannica currency articles

disclaimer: Measured by the year the currency's current name was first adopted for the state's official money and used continuously since. Ties broken alphabetically.
trivia: The British pound sterling traces its lineage to Anglo-Saxon silver pennies of the 8th century, making it the world's oldest currency still in use.

title: Oldest continuously inhabited capital cities
prompt: Name the countries whose current capital city has been continuously inhabited for the longest period.

source.name: Britannica / archaeological records of ancient cities

disclaimer: Measured by earliest archaeological or historical evidence of continuous urban settlement at the site of the modern capital. Traditional founding dates are used where archaeological dates are contested.
trivia: Damascus is widely considered the oldest continuously inhabited capital city, with settlement evidence dating back at least 11,000 years.

title: Oldest active national parks
prompt: Name the countries whose oldest still-active national park was established earliest.

source.name: IUCN / national park service histories

disclaimer: Measured by the founding year of the country's oldest national park that remains protected today. Some earlier reserves that were reclassified or lost protection are excluded.
trivia: Yellowstone, established in 1872, is widely credited as the world's first national park.

title: Longest civil wars
prompt: Name the countries that have endured the longest single civil war in modern history.

source.name: Uppsala Conflict Data Program / Correlates of War

disclaimer: Measured by the total duration in years of the longest single internal armed conflict recognized as a civil war by conflict data programs. Ongoing conflicts are counted through 2024.
trivia: Myanmar's internal conflict, which began shortly after independence in 1948, is often cited as the world's longest ongoing civil war.

title: Longest single military occupations
prompt: Name the countries that endured the longest single military occupation by another state in modern history (post-1800).

source.name: Britannica / academic histories of military occupation

disclaimer: Measured by the duration in years of the longest single continuous military occupation of the country by another sovereign state since 1800. Colonial rule not classified as occupation is excluded.
trivia: The Baltic states endured roughly 50 years of Soviet occupation from 1940 until independence in 1991, one of the longest continuous occupations of the 20th century.

answers.value: 10 years (Allied, 1945-1955 for FRG founding; occupation zones ended)

title: Oldest national anthems
prompt: Name the countries with the oldest officially recognized national anthems (by year the anthem's music or lyrics were adopted).

source.name: Britannica national-anthem articles

disclaimer: Measured by the earliest year the anthem was officially adopted or used ceremonially as the national anthem. Where music predates lyrics or vice versa, the earliest recognized adoption year is used.
trivia: The Dutch 'Wilhelmus' dates to the 1570s, making its melody the oldest of any current national anthem, though it was only formally adopted as the national anthem in 1932.

title: Oldest national flags in current form
prompt: Name the countries whose national flag has been in continuous use in essentially its current form for the longest.

source.name: Flags of the World / national flag registries

disclaimer: Measured by the year the flag's current design elements (colors, symbols, layout) were adopted; minor proportion changes are ignored. Flags redesigned since a major regime change are dated from the new design.
trivia: The Dannebrog, Denmark's red-and-white cross flag, is by tradition the world's oldest continuously used national flag, said to have fallen from the sky in 1219.

title: Oldest continuously operating parliaments
prompt: Name the countries whose national legislative assembly has been continuously operating for the longest period.

source.name: Inter-Parliamentary Union / Britannica parliament histories

disclaimer: Measured by year of establishment of the country's oldest continuously operating national legislative body. Bodies suspended for years by dictatorship, revolution, or foreign occupation are dated from restoration.
trivia: Iceland's Althing, founded in 930 CE at Þingvellir, is widely recognized as the world's oldest surviving parliament.

title: Longest colonial rule endured
prompt: Name the countries that endured the longest continuous period of foreign colonial rule by a European power before independence.

source.name: Britannica / academic colonial histories

disclaimer: Measured by the total years of continuous formal colonial rule by one or more European powers ending at the country's independence date. Nominally independent client states are excluded.
trivia: The Philippines was under Spanish rule for 333 years (1565-1898) before transitioning to nearly 50 years of American administration.

title: Oldest continuously sovereign states
prompt: Name the countries that have maintained continuous sovereign statehood, under an unbroken political entity, for the longest time.

source.name: Britannica / academic state-formation histories

disclaimer: Measured by the year of continuous sovereign statehood under an unbroken political entity, excluding periods of dissolution, foreign conquest, or occupation lasting more than a few years. Traditional founding dates used where academic consensus supports them.
trivia: San Marino, founded in 301 CE according to tradition, claims to be the world's oldest continuously sovereign republic.

answers.value: since 1707 CE (Acts of Union); English kingdom since 927 CE

title: Countries where the most decisive WWII battles were fought
prompt: Name the countries whose modern territory hosted the greatest number of major WWII battles (defined as engagements listed in standard battle-count references).

source.name: Britannica / academic WWII battle indices

disclaimer: Measured by count of major WWII land, air, or naval battles fought on the country's current national territory or coastal waters. Territories that were part of larger empires or occupied states are attributed to the modern successor country. Ties broken alphabetically.
trivia: The Eastern Front saw more major battles than any other WWII theater, with the Soviet Union's territory hosting Stalingrad, Kursk, Moscow, Leningrad, and dozens more decisive engagements.

title: Largest TV advertising markets
prompt: Name the countries with the largest total television advertising revenue.

source.name: GroupM / Dentsu / WARC — Global Ad Trends (TV advertising by country)

disclaimer: TV advertising spend in USD (broadcast + cable + connected TV, excluding pure streaming subscription revenue). Estimates aggregate national broadcaster data via GroupM/WARC.
trivia: The US TV ad market alone is roughly 5x the size of the next-largest, driven in part by political advertising in election years.

title: Most pay-TV subscribers
prompt: Name the countries with the most pay-TV (cable, satellite, and IPTV) subscribers.

source.name: Digital TV Research — Global Pay TV Forecasts

disclaimer: Total pay-TV subscribers across cable, satellite (DTH), and IPTV. Excludes free-to-air television households. India and China dominate on population scale.
trivia: China's pay-TV base is heavily skewed toward digital cable; India's is dominated by DTH satellite due to variable broadband penetration.

title: Most Disney+ subscribers by country
prompt: Name the countries with the most Disney+ paid subscribers.

source.name: Ampere Analysis / Statista — Disney+ subscribers by country

disclaimer: Disney does not publish country-level splits; figures are third-party estimates (Ampere/Kantar). Excludes Disney+ Hotstar bundle in India (separate product).
trivia: Disney+ launched November 2019 in the US and hit 100M subs in 16 months — faster than Netflix, which took over a decade to reach the same figure.

title: Largest SVOD subscriber markets
prompt: Name the countries with the most total streaming (SVOD) subscriptions across all services.

source.name: Digital TV Research — Global SVOD Forecasts

disclaimer: Total SVOD subscriptions across Netflix, Disney+, Amazon Prime Video, HBO Max, local services, etc. Households often hold multiple subscriptions, so counts exceed household totals.
trivia: China's ranking excludes global services (Netflix, Disney+ are blocked); it is powered by domestic platforms iQiyi, Tencent Video, and Youku.

title: Largest ebook markets by revenue
prompt: Name the countries with the largest ebook (digital book) markets by revenue.

source.name: Statista Market Insights — eBooks Worldwide

disclaimer: Consumer ebook retail revenue in USD. Excludes audiobooks and subscription-only services (Kindle Unlimited, Scribd). English-language markets dominate due to earlier Kindle rollout.
trivia: Ebooks represent roughly 20% of total US trade book revenue but under 5% in Germany, where mass-market paperback pricing and cultural preferences favor print.

title: Most International Emmy Award wins
prompt: Name the countries with the most International Emmy Award wins for television programming.

source.name: International Academy of Television Arts & Sciences — Winners archive

disclaimer: Includes International Emmy Awards proper — excludes Primetime Emmys (US) and International Emmy Kids Awards separate categories. Wins credited to country of production.
trivia: The International Emmys were created in 1973 specifically to honor non-US television, since the Primetime Emmys were increasingly US-focused. British productions have long dominated the drama and comedy categories.

title: Most journalists currently imprisoned
prompt: According to the Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ), which countries have the most journalists currently imprisoned?

source.name: Committee to Protect Journalists — Prison Census

disclaimer: CPJ counts journalists jailed for their work as of December 1 of the census year. Excludes those killed, disappeared, or held incommunicado without formal charges.
trivia: CPJ has conducted this census annually since 1990; 2022 set an all-time global record with 363 imprisoned journalists worldwide.

title: Highest daily radio listening time
prompt: Name the countries where people spend the most minutes per day listening to radio.

source.name: Radiocentre / Egta / Nielsen — International radio listening report

disclaimer: Average minutes per day spent listening to broadcast radio (AM/FM/DAB), among the total population aged 15+. Excludes music streaming and podcasts.
trivia: Ireland consistently tops European radio listening charts thanks to strong local station identity and long commute times; RTE Radio 1 alone captures over 20% of daily listeners.

title: Most YouTube channels with 100k+ subscribers
prompt: Name the countries with the most YouTube channels that have surpassed 100,000 subscribers.

source.name: Social Blade / Tubics — YouTube channel demographics

disclaimer: Count of YouTube channels with 100,000+ subscribers registered to each country. Based on Social Blade tracker aggregating channel metadata; excludes channels that hide their country.
trivia: Brazil is famously YouTube-dense on a per-capita basis; Portuguese-language creators face little regional competition and export well to Portugal and Lusophone Africa.

title: Largest OTT/streaming market revenue
prompt: Name the countries with the largest over-the-top (OTT) video streaming market revenue.

source.name: PwC Global Entertainment & Media Outlook — OTT video segment

disclaimer: Total consumer spend on OTT video services in USD (SVOD + TVOD + AVOD revenue). Includes advertising-supported streaming, transactional VOD (rentals/purchases), and subscription streaming.
trivia: The US market alone is roughly 4x the size of the second-largest — Hollywood's global exports drive a majority of the world's OTT catalog value even before local originals are counted.

title: Highest daily TV viewing time
prompt: Name the countries where people spend the most minutes per day watching linear television.

source.name: Eurodata TV Worldwide / Mediametrie — One Television Year in the World

disclaimer: Average minutes per day spent watching live/linear television across all individuals in the measured universe. Excludes streaming, DVR playback beyond same-day, and out-of-home viewing.
trivia: Serbia and much of the Balkans routinely top the global daily TV chart, partly because a large share of entertainment is bundled into inexpensive cable packages rather than paid streaming.

title: Largest book publishing markets
prompt: Name the countries with the largest total book publishing industry revenue.

source.name: International Publishers Association — Annual Report / WIPO

disclaimer: Total net publisher revenue in USD across trade, educational, professional, and academic books (print + digital). Excludes retailer markups.
trivia: China's publishing industry publishes over 500,000 new titles per year (more than any other country) and its net revenue trails only the US despite lower per-copy prices.

title: Largest copper mine producers
prompt: Name the countries with the largest mined copper production.

source.name: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024 — Copper

disclaimer: Ranked by mine production (copper content), not refined production. Values in thousand tonnes.
trivia: Chile has led global copper mining for more than three decades, though its output has slipped as ore grades decline.

title: Largest gold producers
prompt: Name the countries with the largest mined gold production.

source.name: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024 — Gold

disclaimer: Mine production only; excludes recycled scrap. Values in tonnes.
trivia: China has been the world's top gold producer since 2007, though ore grades have been falling and its share of global output is shrinking.

title: Largest natural gas producers
prompt: Name the countries with the largest annual natural gas production.

source.name: U.S. EIA — International Energy Statistics (dry natural gas production)

disclaimer: Marketed dry natural gas production in billion cubic meters (bcm).
trivia: The United States overtook Russia as the world's top natural gas producer in 2011 and has widened its lead as shale output has grown.

title: Largest manganese producers
prompt: Name the countries with the largest manganese ore production.

source.name: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024 — Manganese

disclaimer: Mine production of manganese ore (gross weight), in thousand tonnes.
trivia: South Africa holds about 70% of the world's identified manganese resources — critical for steelmaking and increasingly for lithium-ion battery cathodes.

title: Largest chromium (chromite) producers
prompt: Name the countries with the largest chromite ore production.

source.name: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024 — Chromium

disclaimer: Marketable chromite (gross weight) mine production, in thousand tonnes.
trivia: South Africa alone accounts for roughly 45% of world chromite output, and the country holds the largest identified chromium resources on the planet.

title: Largest tungsten producers
prompt: Name the countries with the largest mined tungsten production.

source.name: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024 — Tungsten

disclaimer: Mine production of tungsten (contained metal), in tonnes.
trivia: China produces over 80% of the world's tungsten and holds more than half of global reserves — a persistent supply concentration flagged in critical-mineral assessments.

title: Largest molybdenum producers
prompt: Name the countries with the largest mined molybdenum production.

source.name: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024 — Molybdenum

disclaimer: Mine production of molybdenum (contained metal), in tonnes.
trivia: Most molybdenum comes as a byproduct of copper mining — which is why the ranking closely tracks the world's top copper-porphyry producers.

title: Largest salt producers
prompt: Name the countries with the largest annual salt production.

source.name: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024 — Salt

disclaimer: Includes rock salt, solar salt, brine, and vacuum salt production. Values in million tonnes.
trivia: China and the United States alternate as world leader most years — U.S. rock salt is dominated by winter road-deicing demand in the Midwest and Northeast.

title: Largest elemental sulfur producers
prompt: Name the countries with the largest annual sulfur production (all forms).

source.name: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024 — Sulfur

disclaimer: Sulfur produced from all sources (Frasch, petroleum, natural gas, metallurgy, pyrite). Values in million tonnes.
trivia: The vast majority of world sulfur is recovered as a byproduct of oil-and-gas refining and metal smelting — very little is still mined directly.

title: Largest gypsum producers
prompt: Name the countries with the largest mined gypsum production.

source.name: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024 — Gypsum

disclaimer: Mine production of crude gypsum, in million tonnes.
trivia: Most mined gypsum ends up as drywall (plasterboard), where it's valued for its natural fire-retardant water-of-crystallization content.

title: Largest magnesite producers
prompt: Name the countries with the largest mined magnesite production.

source.name: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024 — Magnesium Compounds

disclaimer: Mine production of magnesite (magnesium carbonate ore), in thousand tonnes.
trivia: Magnesite is the feedstock for refractory bricks that line steelmaking furnaces — one reason China's dominance here shadows its dominance in steel.

title: Largest natural graphite producers
prompt: Name the countries with the largest mined natural graphite production.

source.name: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024 — Graphite

disclaimer: Natural graphite mine production (flake, amorphous, and vein combined), in thousand tonnes.
trivia: Graphite is a US-designated critical mineral because it's essential to lithium-ion battery anodes — and China refines about 90% of the world's battery-grade material.

title: Largest total retail markets
prompt: Name the countries with the highest total retail sales (all channels combined).

source.name: eMarketer / Insider Intelligence — Global Retail Sales

disclaimer: Total retail sales across all channels (in-store + online), USD at current exchange rates. Excludes fuel and auto dealers.
trivia: China overtook the United States as the world's largest retail market around 2019, and the gap has been widening most years since.

title: Largest Amazon marketplace sales
prompt: Name the countries where Amazon generates the most net sales.

source.name: Amazon.com — 10-K Annual Report, Geographic Segment

disclaimer: Net sales from Amazon's retail marketplaces attributed to each country. Some smaller markets are grouped under 'International' in Amazon's segment reporting; figures are best available public estimates.
trivia: The United States alone accounts for roughly two-thirds of Amazon's global retail net sales, and Germany has been Amazon's largest non-US market for over a decade.

title: Largest cosmetics markets
prompt: Name the countries with the highest total spending on cosmetics and personal care products.

source.name: Statista Market Insights — Beauty & Personal Care

disclaimer: Total revenue of the beauty and personal care market at retail prices, USD at current exchange rates. Includes cosmetics, skin care, fragrances, and personal grooming.
trivia: The United States and China together account for over 40% of global beauty and personal care sales, though South Korea leads the world in per-capita cosmetics spend.

title: Largest pet food markets
prompt: Name the countries with the highest retail pet food sales.

source.name: Euromonitor International — Pet Care

disclaimer: Retail value of dog and cat food sales, USD at current exchange rates. Excludes veterinary diets and pet treats sold outside grocery/pet-specialty channels.
trivia: The United States accounts for roughly a third of global pet food sales — more than Europe combined — and Brazil is the largest pet food market in the Southern Hemisphere.

title: Largest DIY/home-improvement markets
prompt: Name the countries with the highest DIY and home-improvement retail sales.

source.name: European DIY-Retail Association / Statista Home Improvement Outlook

disclaimer: Retail sales of DIY, hardware, and home-improvement stores, USD at current exchange rates. Includes both big-box (Home Depot, B&Q, Bauhaus) and independent hardware retail.
trivia: The United States home-improvement market is larger than all of Europe's combined, driven by the Home Depot / Lowe's duopoly and higher per-household spending on renovation.

title: Highest credit card penetration
prompt: Name the countries with the highest share of adults who own a credit card.

source.name: World Bank — Global Findex Database

disclaimer: Share of adults aged 15+ who report owning a credit card. Excludes debit cards, prepaid cards, and mobile-payment accounts.
trivia: Canada leads the world in credit card ownership — over 80% of Canadian adults hold at least one card, well ahead of the United States.

title: Highest cash use share of transactions
prompt: Name the countries where cash accounts for the largest share of point-of-sale payments.

source.name: Worldpay/FIS — Global Payments Report

disclaimer: Cash share of in-person point-of-sale transaction value. Excludes e-commerce. Countries with very small POS markets excluded.
trivia: Japan and Germany are famously cash-loyal advanced economies — over half of in-store payments in both are still made with physical cash.

title: Highest buy-now-pay-later share
prompt: Name the countries where buy-now-pay-later (BNPL) accounts for the largest share of e-commerce spending.

source.name: Worldpay/FIS — Global Payments Report

disclaimer: BNPL share of e-commerce transaction value. Includes services like Klarna, Afterpay, Affirm, and Zip.
trivia: BNPL took off first in the Nordics — Sweden's Klarna essentially invented the modern category — and Sweden, Norway, and Germany remain the world's most BNPL-heavy markets.

title: Most e-cigarette users
prompt: Name the countries with the most adults who use e-cigarettes or vaping products.

source.name: World Health Organization / Euromonitor Vapor Products

disclaimer: Estimated number of current adult e-cigarette users. Excludes heated-tobacco products (IQOS-style) and traditional cigarettes.
trivia: The United States, China, and the United Kingdom together account for more than half of the world's e-cigarette users, and the UK actively promotes vaping as a smoking-cessation tool.

title: Most vending machines per capita
prompt: Name the countries with the most vending machines per capita.

source.name: European Vending & Coffee Service Association / Japan Vending Machine Manufacturers Association

disclaimer: Total installed vending machines divided by population. Includes drink, food, and non-food machines.
trivia: Japan has one vending machine for roughly every 30 people — the highest density in the world — driven by low vandalism, dense cities, and the machines' cultural ubiquity for hot and cold drinks.

title: Most convenience stores
prompt: Name the countries with the most convenience stores in operation.

source.name: NACS — Global Convenience Store Count

disclaimer: Number of convenience stores (including chain and independent) as tracked by NACS and national retail associations. Excludes small groceries that aren't classified as c-stores.
trivia: China leads the world in total convenience store count, but Japan and South Korea have the highest densities — a c-store is within walking distance of nearly every urban address in both countries.

title: Largest baby-goods markets
prompt: Name the countries with the highest retail spending on baby and infant goods.

source.name: Euromonitor International — Baby and Child-Specific Products

disclaimer: Retail value of baby and child-specific products (formula, diapers, baby food, skincare, apparel), USD at current exchange rates.
trivia: China's baby-goods market briefly overtook the United States in the mid-2010s during the two-child policy relaxation, but slowing birth rates have pushed the US back to #1.

title: Highest interpersonal trust
prompt: Name the countries where the highest share of people say 'most people can be trusted' in the World Values Survey / OECD Trust indicator.

source.name: OECD Trust in others (WVS aggregated)

disclaimer: Metric is the share of respondents answering 'most people can be trusted' rather than 'can't be too careful' in the World Values Survey wave 7 / OECD Better Life data.
trivia: Nordic countries dominate the top of interpersonal trust rankings — a phenomenon researchers link to strong universal welfare systems and low corruption.

title: Highest volunteering rate
prompt: Name the countries with the highest share of people who volunteered time to an organization in the past month (CAF World Giving Index).

source.name: Charities Aid Foundation — World Giving Index 2023

disclaimer: Measures the share of respondents who volunteered time to a charitable or non-profit organization in the past month; the CAF sub-index is one of three components in the overall giving score.
trivia: Liberia and Kenya routinely top the volunteering sub-index despite low income — much of the activity is community mutual-aid work outside formal NGOs.

title: Highest 'helped a stranger' rate
prompt: Name the countries with the highest share of people who reported helping a stranger in the past month (CAF World Giving Index).

source.name: Charities Aid Foundation — World Giving Index 2023

disclaimer: Measures Gallup survey respondents answering yes to 'have you helped a stranger, or someone you didn't know who needed help, in the last month?' — one of three CAF sub-indices.
trivia: Jamaica, Liberia, and Libya have topped the 'helping a stranger' index in recent years — the metric captures informal generosity that formal charity rankings often miss.

title: Highest share of vegetarians
prompt: Name the countries with the highest share of the population identifying as vegetarian.

source.name: Ipsos Global Advisor / national dietary surveys (aggregated)

disclaimer: Ranks by share of population identifying as vegetarian; excludes flexitarians and pescatarians. India's share dwarfs other countries due to religious dietary tradition.
trivia: Roughly 30 percent of Indian adults describe themselves as strictly vegetarian, more than any other country by a wide margin — the second-ranked country doesn't reach half that share.

title: Highest share of vegans
prompt: Name the countries with the highest share of the population identifying as vegan.

source.name: Ipsos Global Advisor / national dietary surveys

disclaimer: Share of population identifying as strictly vegan (excludes plant-based flexitarians and vegetarians who consume dairy).
trivia: Israel routinely tops per-capita vegan rankings, with Tel Aviv often called the 'vegan capital of the world' — the movement is driven by both animal-welfare and religious kosher considerations.

title: Highest LGBT+ Equality Index
prompt: Name the countries with the highest score on the Equaldex LGBT+ Equality Index (legal rights + public opinion).

source.name: Equaldex — LGBT+ Equality Index

disclaimer: The Equaldex Equality Index is a composite score (0-100) combining legal recognition of LGBT+ rights (marriage, adoption, discrimination protections, etc.) and public opinion polling.
trivia: Iceland has led the Equaldex ranking since 2022, edging out longtime leader the Netherlands — Iceland's parliament unanimously legalised same-sex marriage in 2010.

title: Highest home ownership rate
prompt: Name the countries with the highest share of households that own (rather than rent) their home.

source.name: Eurostat, Trading Economics, national statistics offices

disclaimer: Share of households living in owner-occupied dwellings (with or without an outstanding mortgage). Sources vary slightly year-to-year; Eastern Europe consistently dominates the top of the list due to post-communist privatisation of state housing.
trivia: Romania has one of the highest home ownership rates in the world (over 95%) because state housing was mass-privatised to sitting tenants at nominal prices in the early 1990s.

title: Most museums by country
prompt: Name the countries with the largest total number of museums.

source.name: UNESCO Institute for Statistics / national museum registries

disclaimer: Total number of museums as reported to UNESCO and by national museum associations; definitions vary but generally include public, private, and specialty museums registered with a governing body.
trivia: Germany's museum count is inflated by its long tradition of municipal Heimatmuseums — small local-history museums that most cities and towns run out of civic pride.

title: Highest Rule of Law Index
prompt: Name the countries with the highest score on the World Justice Project Rule of Law Index.

source.name: World Justice Project — Rule of Law Index

disclaimer: Composite score (0-1) across eight factors: constraints on government, absence of corruption, open government, fundamental rights, order & security, regulatory enforcement, civil justice, and criminal justice.
trivia: Denmark has ranked #1 on the Rule of Law Index every year since 2015 — the WJP notes it scores in the top 5 on all eight sub-factors.

title: Highest weekly religious service attendance
prompt: Name the countries where the highest share of adults report attending religious services at least once a week (Pew/WVS surveys).

source.name: Pew Research Center — Religiosity data / World Values Survey

disclaimer: Share of adults reporting weekly or more frequent attendance at religious services; covers all religions. Data from Pew Global Attitudes and WVS wave 7.
trivia: Nigeria's weekly religious attendance is one of the highest in the world, split fairly evenly between Christian and Muslim worshippers.

title: Highest Freedom in the World score
prompt: Name the countries with the highest total score on Freedom House's Freedom in the World civil/political liberties index.

source.name: Freedom House — Freedom in the World 2024

disclaimer: Aggregate score out of 100, combining political rights (out of 40) and civil liberties (out of 60). Ties are common at the top of the list; broken alphabetically.
trivia: Finland, Norway, Sweden, and New Zealand have tied at or near the top of Freedom in the World every year since 2016 — all four score perfect 40s on political rights.

title: Highest civic engagement
prompt: Name the countries with the highest score on the OECD Better Life Index civic engagement domain (voter turnout + stakeholder engagement).

source.name: OECD Better Life Index — Civic Engagement

disclaimer: OECD Better Life civic engagement domain combines voter turnout in the most recent national election with stakeholder engagement in developing laws and regulations. Score out of 10.
trivia: Australia's civic engagement score is boosted by compulsory voting, which pushes voter turnout above 90% at every federal election.

title: Most FIVB Men's Volleyball World Championship titles

title: Most Men's Elite Road Race UCI World titles
prompt: Name the countries whose riders have won the most UCI Road World Championships elite men's road race titles.

source.name: UCI — Road World Championships

disclaimer: Only the professional/elite men's road race event is counted (not amateur or time trial). Great Britain aggregates constituent-nation riders where applicable.
trivia: Belgium and Italy alone account for more than half of all men's elite road race world titles ever awarded, and Eddy Merckx and Alfredo Binda each won it three times individually.

title: Most MotoGP premier class world titles
prompt: Name the countries whose riders have won the most premier-class Grand Prix motorcycle world championships (500cc / MotoGP combined).

source.name: MotoGP — 500cc / MotoGP champions list

disclaimer: Combines pre-2002 500cc titles with post-2002 MotoGP titles. Attribution is by rider nationality, not manufacturer.
trivia: Italy and Spain together account for more than half of premier-class titles, and Giacomo Agostini (ITA) won 8 of Italy's total on his own.

title: Most IJF Judo World Championship gold medals
prompt: Name the countries with the most gold medals at the IJF World Judo Championships (all senior weight categories).

source.name: IJF — World Judo Championships medal table

disclaimer: All-time senior individual golds since the event's founding in 1956. Team event and youth categories excluded. Soviet Union golds counted under Russia.
trivia: Japan has won more world titles than the next three nations combined, and Ryoko Tani (JPN) alone won seven world golds across her career.

title: Most Taekwondo World Championship gold medals
prompt: Name the countries with the most gold medals at the World Taekwondo Championships (senior, all weight categories).

source.name: World Taekwondo — World Championships medal table

disclaimer: All-time senior individual golds since 1973. Combines men's and women's kyorugi categories. Team and Poomsae events excluded.

title: Most FIE Fencing World Championship gold medals
prompt: Name the countries with the most gold medals at the FIE Fencing World Championships (individual and team, all weapons combined).

source.name: FIE — World Fencing Championships medal table

trivia: Italy and France have swapped the top of the fencing medal table for a century — the first World Championships were held in Paris in 1921.

title: Most Men's Water Polo World Championship titles
prompt: Name the countries with the most gold medals at the FINA/World Aquatics Men's Water Polo World Championship.

source.name: World Aquatics — Men's Water Polo World Championship history

disclaimer: Only the men's tournament held at the Aquatics World Championships (from 1973). Yugoslavia titles are counted under Serbia as successor; Soviet Union under Russia.
trivia: Hungary won three of the first five men's world titles and the sport's most decorated player, Tibor Benedek, was on the 2003 gold-winning squad.

title: Most IIHF Ice Hockey World Championship gold medals
prompt: Name the countries with the most gold medals at the IIHF Men's Ice Hockey World Championship.

source.name: IIHF — Men's Ice Hockey World Championship history

disclaimer: Cumulative senior men's IIHF World Championship gold medals from 1920 (originally held at the Olympics) through the most recent edition. Soviet Union titles aggregated under Russia; Czechoslovakia's titles counted under Czechia.
trivia: Canada is the only country to have played at every IIHF Ice Hockey World Championship, and the USSR/Russia line and Canada together account for more than half of all men's world titles.

title: Most Men's Curling World Championship titles
prompt: Name the countries with the most gold medals at the World Men's Curling Championship.

source.name: World Curling Federation — Men's World Championship history

disclaimer: Only the annual World Men's Curling Championship (from 1959, originally the Scotch Cup). Scotland's titles are aggregated under Great Britain per the standard convention.
trivia: Canada has won more men's world curling titles than every other nation on Earth combined, and Randy Ferbey (CAN) alone skipped four world championship winning teams.

title: Most UCI Track Cycling World Championship golds
prompt: Name the countries with the most all-time gold medals at the UCI Track Cycling World Championships (men and women combined).

source.name: UCI — Track Cycling World Championships medal table

title: Most FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup medals
prompt: Name the countries with the most all-time medals at the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup.

title: Most FIFA Beach Soccer World Cup medals

title: Most IWF Weightlifting World Championship golds

trivia: The USSR and China alone account for a majority of all-time weightlifting world titles, and China's Chen Yanqing won six world championship golds across four weight classes.

title: Most WKF Karate World Championship golds
prompt: Name the countries with the most all-time gold medals at the WKF Karate World Championships (senior, all events).

source.name: WKF — Karate World Championships medal table

disclaimer: Combined senior gold medals across all kumite weight categories and kata (individual and team) since the event's founding in 1970. Youth and junior championships excluded.

title: Most FIS Freestyle Skiing World Championship medals
prompt: Name the countries with the most all-time medals at the FIS Freestyle Ski World Championships (all disciplines).

source.name: FIS — Freestyle Ski World Championships medal table

disclaimer: Combined golds, silvers and bronzes across all freestyle disciplines (moguls, aerials, ski cross, halfpipe, slopestyle, big air) since 1986. Freestyle only; alpine and cross-country skiing excluded.

title: Most international tourist arrivals
prompt: Name the countries that receive the most inbound international tourist arrivals per year.

source.name: UN Tourism (UNWTO) — International Tourism Highlights

disclaimer: Counts overnight visitors crossing an international border for tourism. Same-day (excursionist) visitors are excluded.

title: Tourism's biggest share of GDP
