title: Most 5-star hotels
prompt: Name the countries with the largest number of 5-star / luxury-tier hotel properties.

source.name: Statista / STR Global — Luxury hotel inventory by country

disclaimer: Counts hotel properties classified at the top luxury tier by national rating bodies or STR's chain-scale definition. Definitions of '5-star' vary slightly across countries.
trivia: China leapt into the top tier of luxury hotel supply during the 2010s as domestic chains like Shangri-La and Wanda opened hundreds of properties.

title: Most theme park visitors
prompt: Name the countries hosting the world's top-25 most-visited amusement/theme parks, ranked by aggregate annual attendance.

source.name: TEA / AECOM Theme Index — Top 25 Amusement/Theme Parks Worldwide

disclaimer: Sums attendance at the top-25 global amusement/theme parks by the country each park is located in. Water parks and standalone attractions are excluded.
trivia: Walt Disney World's Magic Kingdom alone drew over 17 million visitors in 2023, more than the entire annual attendance of most European park operators combined.

title: Largest casino gambling markets
prompt: Name the countries with the highest total casino gaming revenue (gross gaming revenue, USD).

source.name: American Gaming Association / H2 Gambling Capital — Global casino GGR by market

disclaimer: Land-based casino gross gaming revenue in USD. Online gambling, sports betting, and lotteries excluded. Macao is reported separately by its Gaming Inspection Bureau.
trivia: Macao overtook the Las Vegas Strip as the world's top casino market in 2007, and its 2023 rebound after COVID reopening was the fastest recovery in the industry.

title: Most ski resorts
prompt: Name the countries with the largest number of operating ski resorts.

source.name: Vanat International Report on Snow & Mountain Tourism

disclaimer: Counts distinct commercial ski areas with at least one mechanical lift. Includes both alpine and Nordic resorts.
trivia: Japan has more ski resorts than any single Alpine nation, though most are small operations serving domestic day-trippers rather than international destinations.

title: Safest countries for tourists
prompt: Name the countries ranked safest overall on the Global Peace Index, a proxy commonly used for travel-safety.

source.name: Institute for Economics & Peace — Global Peace Index

disclaimer: Rank 1 = safest. Composite of 23 indicators including violent crime, terrorism, political stability, and militarization. Not a tourism-specific index but widely cited by travel-safety advisories.
trivia: Iceland has topped the Global Peace Index every year since the ranking began in 2008.

title: Most Blue Flag beaches
prompt: Name the countries with the most Blue Flag-certified beaches (ecolabel awarded for water quality and environmental management).

source.name: Foundation for Environmental Education — Blue Flag Programme

disclaimer: Counts Blue Flag-certified beaches only; marinas and sustainable boating operators are excluded. Awarded annually and must be re-earned each year.
trivia: Spain has held the top spot for Blue Flag beaches for over three decades, currently certifying more than 630 beaches, marinas, and vessels combined.

title: Largest wellness tourism markets
prompt: Name the countries with the largest wellness-tourism markets (spending on spa, health-retreat, and wellness-focused travel).

source.name: Global Wellness Institute — Wellness Economy Monitor

disclaimer: Wellness tourism spending in USD, covering trips primarily motivated by wellness activities plus wellness-adjacent secondary spending on regular trips.
trivia: The United States accounts for over a third of the global wellness tourism market by dollar value, driven by high-end spa resorts in California, Arizona, and Colorado.

title: Most international association meetings hosted
prompt: Name the countries that host the most international association meetings, the standard measure of the MICE (meetings, incentives, conferences, exhibitions) business-tourism sector.

source.name: ICCA — International Congress and Convention Association Country Rankings

disclaimer: Counts qualifying international association meetings held in each country during the reporting year. Corporate-only meetings and one-country association events are excluded.
trivia: The United States has led the ICCA country rankings almost every year since the association began publishing them in 1963.

title: Most-searched travel destinations
prompt: Name the countries most-searched on Google Flights and Google Search as travel destinations.

source.name: Google Trends / Google Destination Insights — Year in Search Travel

disclaimer: Aggregates worldwide search interest for country-as-destination queries. Reflects consideration, not actual visitor volume; heavily weighted to English-language traffic.
trivia: Japan surged in search interest after its post-COVID border reopening in late 2022, briefly becoming the world's most-searched destination on Google Flights.

title: Most cruise passenger embarkations
prompt: Name the countries whose ports handle the most cruise passenger embarkations (turnaround / homeport departures, not port-of-call visits).

source.name: Cruise Lines International Association (CLIA) — State of the Cruise Industry

disclaimer: Counts passengers boarding cruise ships to begin voyages (homeport turnarounds). Distinct from cruise port-of-call arrivals where passengers only disembark briefly.
trivia: Miami's PortMiami alone accounts for more cruise passenger embarkations than any other single port in the world, giving the U.S. a dominant share of global cruise turnaround traffic.

title: Longest paved road network
prompt: Name the countries with the longest paved road networks.

source.name: CIA World Factbook — Roadways (paved)

disclaimer: Measures paved road length only (not total road length including unpaved). Latest CIA World Factbook figures, several reporting years due to inconsistent updates by country.
trivia: The United States has more paved roads than the next three countries combined; China's rapid expressway build-out over the last two decades has vaulted it past India to second place.

title: Most metro/subway stations
prompt: Name the countries with the most metro (rapid-transit) stations across all their cities combined.

source.name: UITP — World Metro Figures / Metro Bits

disclaimer: Sum of stations across all rapid-transit (metro/subway) systems in the country. Excludes commuter rail, light rail, and trams.
trivia: China has added more metro stations in the last 15 years than the rest of the world combined; roughly 45 Chinese cities now operate metro systems.

title: Most bicycles per capita
prompt: Name the countries with the most bicycles per person.

source.name: World Economic Forum / Statista — Bicycle ownership by country

disclaimer: Bicycles owned per person (ratio, 0-1). Household-survey based; figures vary somewhat across sources.
trivia: Denmark and the Netherlands both have more bikes than people, and Copenhagen alone counts more bicycles than cars on its streets.

title: Most motorcycles per capita
prompt: Name the countries with the most motorcycles and scooters per person.

source.name: Pew Research Center / ACEM — Motorcycle ownership by country

disclaimer: Motorcycles and mopeds/scooters registered per 1,000 inhabitants. Includes both electric and combustion two-wheelers.
trivia: In Vietnam, motorbikes account for over 90% of registered vehicles, and Hanoi has more registered two-wheelers than residents.

title: Most EV charging points
prompt: Name the countries with the most public electric-vehicle charging points installed.

source.name: IEA — Global EV Outlook 2024

disclaimer: Total publicly accessible EV charging points (slow + fast). Private/home chargers excluded. IEA definitions.
trivia: China operates more public chargers than the rest of the world combined, and about 70% of the world's public fast chargers are located there.

title: Most passenger cars produced
prompt: Name the countries that produce the most passenger cars per year.

source.name: OICA — International Organization of Motor Vehicle Manufacturers, Production Statistics

disclaimer: Passenger cars only, not commercial vehicles. Annual production by country of assembly (not manufacturer HQ).
trivia: China alone produced more passenger cars in 2023 than the entire European Union combined, and it overtook Japan as the world's top car exporter in the same year.

title: Most commercial vehicles produced
prompt: Name the countries that produce the most commercial vehicles (trucks, vans, buses) per year.

source.name: OICA — Production Statistics (Commercial vehicles)

disclaimer: Commercial vehicles = light commercial vehicles, heavy trucks, buses and coaches. Excludes passenger cars.
trivia: The US tops this list because most pickup trucks are classified as light commercial vehicles rather than passenger cars — flip the OICA definition and China would lead instead.

title: Longest navigable inland waterways
prompt: Name the countries with the longest navigable inland waterways (rivers, canals, and lakes usable for transport).

source.name: CIA World Factbook — Waterways

disclaimer: Total length of waterways navigable by ocean-going vessels or shallow-draft boats, per CIA World Factbook definitions. Includes rivers, canals, and lakes.
trivia: China's figure is dominated by the Yangtze and the ancient Grand Canal, which at over 1,700 km is still the world's longest man-made waterway.

title: Highest total port cargo throughput
prompt: Name the countries whose ports handle the most cargo tonnage per year (all cargo types combined).

source.name: UNCTAD — Review of Maritime Transport

disclaimer: Total port cargo throughput in million metric tons, all cargo types (dry bulk, liquid bulk, containers, general cargo). Differs from container-only TEU rankings.
trivia: Seven of the world's ten busiest ports by tonnage are in China; Ningbo-Zhoushan alone handles more cargo tonnage than any other single port in history.

title: Most tram and light-rail systems
prompt: Name the countries with the most tram or light-rail systems in operation.

source.name: UITP / LRTA — World Tramway and Light Rail Systems Directory

disclaimer: Count of operating urban tramway and light-rail systems by country. Historic heritage-only tourist lines excluded.
trivia: Germany kept almost all its trams running through the 20th century while much of the world tore theirs up, and it still operates more networks than any other country by a wide margin.

title: Most cars per capita
prompt: Name the countries with the most passenger cars per person (excluding trucks, buses, and other commercial vehicles).

source.name: OICA / Eurostat — Passenger cars in use per capita

disclaimer: Passenger cars in use per 1,000 inhabitants. Excludes light trucks, SUVs classified as light commercial, and heavier vehicles. Distinct from motor-vehicles-per-capita, which includes all vehicle classes.
trivia: San Marino tops the list not because of local demand but because its low registration fees attract owners from across northern Italy.

title: Largest civil aviation fleet
prompt: Name the countries with the most commercial passenger and cargo aircraft registered.

source.name: ICAO / FlightGlobal World Airliner Census

disclaimer: In-service commercial jets and turboprops registered to the country's airlines. Excludes military aircraft and general-aviation single-engine planes.
trivia: US carriers operate roughly a quarter of the world's commercial aircraft; American Airlines alone flies more planes than the entire national fleets of most European countries.

title: Most Named Mountain Peaks
prompt: Name the US states with the most named mountain peaks catalogued in the USGS Geographic Names Information System (GNIS).

source.name: USGS Geographic Names Information System (GNIS) — feature class 'Summit'

disclaimer: Counts of GNIS features with feature class 'Summit' by state. Every named summit is counted regardless of elevation. Includes Washington DC.
trivia: Nevada's Basin and Range topography produces thousands of small isolated peaks, giving it far more named summits than states with higher but more contiguous ranges.

title: Most Named Peaks Over 5,000 ft
prompt: Name the US states with the most named summits above 5,000 feet in elevation.

source.name: Peakbagger.com — state summit databases

disclaimer: Named summits above 5,000 ft (1,524 m) with recognized names in Peakbagger's state databases. Elevation cutoff is fixed, not prominence-adjusted. DC not included (source omits it).
trivia: Colorado's 5,000-ft threshold catches essentially every named peak in the state — its lowest point (the Arikaree River) sits at 3,317 ft.

title: Largest Tribal Land Area
prompt: Name the US states with the largest total area of federally recognized tribal (reservation and trust) lands.

source.name: US Bureau of Indian Affairs / US Census Bureau — American Indian Areas

disclaimer: Total land area of federally recognized American Indian reservations plus off-reservation trust lands within each state's boundaries. DC not included (source omits it).
trivia: Arizona's tribal land total is driven mostly by the Navajo Nation, which spans three states and has its capital at Window Rock.

title: Largest Reservoir Storage Capacity
prompt: Name the US states with the largest total surface-water reservoir storage capacity.

source.name: US Army Corps of Engineers — National Inventory of Dams (NID)

disclaimer: Sum of maximum normal storage across all dams in each state as recorded in the National Inventory of Dams. Interstate reservoirs are credited to the state hosting the dam. Includes Washington DC.
trivia: Nevada's chart-topping storage comes almost entirely from Lake Mead behind Hoover Dam, the largest reservoir by capacity in the United States.

title: Most Named Waterfalls
prompt: Name the US states with the most named waterfalls catalogued in the USGS Geographic Names Information System.

source.name: USGS Geographic Names Information System (GNIS) — feature class 'Falls'

disclaimer: Counts of GNIS features classified as 'Falls' by state. Includes all named cascades regardless of drop height. DC not included (source omits it).
trivia: Washington's Cascade and Olympic ranges produce so many named falls that the state is often called the Waterfall Capital of the Lower 48.

title: Largest Rangeland (Grassland) Area
prompt: Name the US states with the largest total area of rangeland (native grassland, shrubland, and open range).

source.name: USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service — Natural Resources Inventory

disclaimer: Non-federal plus federal rangeland acres as classified by NRCS. Rangeland is distinct from cropland and pastureland. DC not included (source omits it).
trivia: Texas contains more rangeland than the next two states combined, spanning from the Chihuahuan Desert scrub in the west to the coastal prairie in the south.

title: Largest Coniferous Forest Area
prompt: Name the US states with the largest area of coniferous (softwood) forest.

source.name: USDA Forest Service — Forest Inventory and Analysis (FIA)

disclaimer: Timberland and other forestland classified by FIA as softwood forest-type groups (pine, fir, spruce, hemlock, cedar, redwood). Alaska's boreal forests are included. DC not included (source omits it).
trivia: Oregon's Douglas-fir forests west of the Cascades produce more softwood timber volume per acre than almost anywhere else in the country.

title: Largest Island Area Under State Jurisdiction
prompt: Name the US states with the largest total land area of islands (river, lake, coastal, and offshore) under their jurisdiction.

source.name: USGS National Hydrography Dataset — Island features

disclaimer: Total land area of all islands lying within a state's legal boundaries, including inhabited and uninhabited islands in oceans, gulfs, sounds, lakes, and rivers. DC not included (topic is state-scoped).
trivia: Hawaii's island area is essentially the entire state — every square mile of Hawaiian land is on an island.

title: Most Named Barrier Islands
prompt: Name the US states with the most named barrier islands along their coasts.

source.name: USGS Coastal and Marine Geology Program — Barrier Island inventory

disclaimer: Named barrier islands as inventoried by USGS coastal geology surveys. Excludes barrier spits still attached to the mainland. DC not included (source omits it).
trivia: Florida has more named barrier islands than any other state, with clusters running the entire length of both its Atlantic and Gulf coastlines.

title: Most Named Canyons
prompt: Name the US states with the most named canyons catalogued in the USGS Geographic Names Information System.

source.name: USGS Geographic Names Information System (GNIS) — feature class 'Valley' filtered to canyon names

disclaimer: Counts of GNIS features whose names include 'Canyon' by state. Reflects naming convention as much as underlying topography. DC not included (source omits it).
trivia: Utah's dry climate and thick sedimentary rock layers make it the canyon-country capital of the U.S., with more named canyons than any other state.

title: Longest River Wholly Within Borders
prompt: Name the US states with the longest single river that flows entirely within their own borders.

source.name: USGS National Hydrography Dataset — river length by state

disclaimer: Longest single named river whose entire course lies within one state's boundaries. Rivers that cross state lines are excluded. Includes Washington DC.
trivia: Alaska's Kuskokwim River flows 702 miles from the Kuskokwim Mountains to the Bering Sea, all within Alaska, making it the longest single-state river in the U.S.

title: Most Named Plateaus
prompt: Name the US states with the most named plateaus catalogued in the USGS Geographic Names Information System.

source.name: USGS Geographic Names Information System (GNIS) — feature class 'Flat' filtered to plateau/mesa names

disclaimer: Counts of GNIS features whose names include 'Plateau' or 'Mesa' by state. Reflects Southwestern mesa-country naming density. DC not included (source omits it).
trivia: Arizona's Colorado Plateau country is dotted with hundreds of named mesas, from Black Mesa to First Mesa to Grand Mesa.

title: Most Named Bays
prompt: Name the US states with the most named bays catalogued in the USGS Geographic Names Information System.

source.name: USGS Geographic Names Information System (GNIS) — feature class 'Bay'

disclaimer: Counts of GNIS features classified as 'Bay' by state, including tidal, lake, and river bays. Includes Washington DC.
trivia: Alaska's coastline is roughly half the U.S. total, and its named bays outnumber every other state's by an order of magnitude.

title: Most Named Sounds
prompt: Name the US states with the most named sounds (elongated coastal or inland water bodies) catalogued in the USGS GNIS.

source.name: USGS Geographic Names Information System (GNIS) — feature class 'Channel/Sound'

disclaimer: Counts of GNIS features whose names include 'Sound' by state, covering marine straits between islands and mainland as well as broad estuarine passages. DC not included (source omits it).
trivia: Alaska's fjord-and-island geography produces more named sounds than the rest of the U.S. combined — Prince William Sound is only one of hundreds.

title: Largest Peak Snowpack (SWE)
prompt: Name the US states with the largest peak-season snowpack, measured as snow water equivalent (SWE) averaged across NRCS SNOTEL sites.

source.name: USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service — SNOTEL network

disclaimer: Average April 1 snow water equivalent across all SNOTEL sites in each state. April 1 is the traditional peak for the Western U.S. snowpack cycle. DC not included (topic is state-scoped).
trivia: Alaska tops the list because its SNOTEL sites sit in maritime coastal ranges where 40-60 inches of snow water equivalent accumulate each winter.

title: Most Craft Distilleries
prompt: Name the US states with the most licensed craft distilleries.

source.name: American Craft Spirits Association — Annual Economic Impact Report

disclaimer: Count of DSP-licensed craft distilleries operating in each state (ACSA definition). Includes Washington DC.
trivia: New York overtook California in the late 2010s after a state farm-distillery license law dramatically lowered fees for small producers.

title: Most Wineries
prompt: Name the US states with the most bonded wineries.

source.name: Wines Vines Analytics — Winery Database

disclaimer: Bonded winery count includes all TTB-permitted winery premises, from major producers to boutique operations. DC not included (source omits it).
trivia: California has more bonded wineries than the next four states combined, though Washington's Columbia Valley leads by acreage growth.

title: Most Farmers Markets
prompt: Name the US states with the most farmers markets registered with the USDA.

source.name: USDA AMS — National Farmers Market Directory

disclaimer: Total count of currently listed farmers markets in the USDA Local Food Portal directory. Includes Washington DC.
trivia: New York's total is driven by NYC Greenmarkets plus a dense network of upstate seasonal markets promoted by the state Ag Department.

title: Highest EV Share of New Vehicle Sales
prompt: Name the US states where electric vehicles make up the highest share of new light-duty vehicle registrations.

source.name: Alliance for Automotive Innovation — Get Connected EV Report

disclaimer: Battery-electric vehicles as share of new light-duty registrations; hybrids and plug-in hybrids excluded. Includes Washington DC.
trivia: California's ZEV mandate and its 15-state Section 177 followers drive most of the top of this list.

title: Most Utility-Scale Solar Capacity Installed
prompt: Name the US states with the most installed utility-scale solar electricity generating capacity.

source.name: SEIA / Wood Mackenzie — US Solar Market Insight

disclaimer: Cumulative installed utility-scale + distributed PV capacity in gigawatts (AC-DC mixed by SEIA convention).
trivia: Texas overtook California as the annual installation leader in 2022 and is on pace to surpass total California capacity by the late 2020s.

title: Most Wind Capacity Installed
prompt: Name the US states with the most installed wind electricity generating capacity.

source.name: US Energy Information Administration — Electricity Data Browser

disclaimer: Cumulative installed onshore + offshore wind nameplate capacity in gigawatts. DC not included (topic is state-scoped).
trivia: Texas has more installed wind capacity than the next three states combined, and about half of the state's grid is served by wind on peak nights.

title: Highest Residential Electricity Price
prompt: Name the US states with the highest average residential electricity price.

source.name: US Energy Information Administration — Electric Power Monthly Table 5.6.A

disclaimer: Average residential retail price of electricity in cents per kilowatt-hour, all sectors annualized. Includes Washington DC.
trivia: Hawaii's price is nearly triple the national average because the islands generate most of their electricity from imported petroleum.

title: Most ZIP Codes
prompt: Name the US states with the most ZIP codes assigned by the US Postal Service.

source.name: USPS ZIP Code Directory (aggregated by UnitedStatesZipCodes.org)

disclaimer: Total count includes standard, PO Box, unique (single-recipient) and military ZIP codes. Includes Washington DC.
trivia: Texas has the most ZIP codes despite California having a larger population, thanks to the state's dispersed rural post office network.

title: Most Licensed Drivers
prompt: Name the US states with the most licensed drivers.

source.name: US Federal Highway Administration — Highway Statistics Series Table DL-1C

disclaimer: Count of active licensed drivers (all classes) by state of residence, in millions. Includes Washington DC.
trivia: California has more licensed drivers than the combined populations of the 20 smallest states.

title: Highest Firearm Death Rate
prompt: Name the US states with the highest age-adjusted firearm death rate.

source.name: CDC WONDER — Firearm Mortality by State

disclaimer: Deaths from all firearm-related injuries (suicide, homicide, accidental) per 100,000 residents, age-adjusted. Includes Washington DC.
trivia: Suicides consistently account for over half of firearm deaths nationally, and drive the ranking in most of the top-10 states.

title: Most Bird Species Observed
prompt: Name the US states with the most bird species ever observed and accepted by state records committees.

source.name: American Birding Association / eBird State Totals

disclaimer: Cumulative all-time count of species accepted on official state checklists. Includes Washington DC.
trivia: Texas leads because migration corridors from three flyways converge on the Gulf Coast, funneling neotropical species through the state each spring.

title: Most Native American Reservation Land Area
prompt: Name the US states with the most Native American reservation and trust land area.

source.name: US Bureau of Indian Affairs — Land Area Representation Data

disclaimer: Total federal trust and reservation acreage held for tribes and individuals; excludes Alaska Native Corporation lands (ANCSA) which have a different legal status. Includes Washington DC.
trivia: Arizona edges Alaska because most Alaska Native land was converted to corporate ownership under the 1971 ANCSA settlement rather than held as reservations.

title: Most H-1B Approvals
prompt: Name the US states where the most H-1B specialty-occupation petitions are approved.

source.name: USCIS — H-1B Employer Data Hub

disclaimer: Number of initial + continuing H-1B approvals for beneficiaries whose worksite is located in each state. Includes Washington DC.
trivia: California and Texas together account for roughly a third of all H-1B approvals nationally, reflecting the concentration of tech and consulting employers.

title: Most Pickleball Courts
prompt: Name the US states with the most known pickleball courts (dedicated + shared-use lined).

source.name: USA Pickleball — Places2Play Directory

disclaimer: Total known playable courts including dedicated pickleball courts and tennis/multi-use courts lined for pickleball. Includes Washington DC.
trivia: Florida leads on a per-capita and total basis; the sport's fastest early growth came from active-adult retirement communities in the Sun Belt.

title: Highest DUI Arrest Rate
prompt: Name the US states with the highest rate of DUI arrests per 100,000 residents.

source.name: FBI Uniform Crime Reporting — Crime in the US, Arrests by State

disclaimer: Driving-under-the-influence arrests per 100,000 residents. Rates reflect enforcement intensity and legal thresholds as much as underlying impaired-driving prevalence. Includes Washington DC.
trivia: Sparse-population Western states with strong highway patrols tend to top the list; South Dakota's high number reflects Sturgis rally enforcement.

title: Most Operating Nuclear Reactors
prompt: Name the US states with the most commercial nuclear power reactors currently in operation, from most to fewest.

source.name: US Nuclear Regulatory Commission — Operating Reactors

disclaimer: Counts operating commercial reactors licensed by the NRC; excludes research reactors and units in decommissioning. DC not included (source omits it).
trivia: Illinois hosts more nuclear reactors than any other state, and gets a larger share of its electricity from nuclear than any other state (~54%).

title: Highest Coal Share of Electricity Generation
prompt: Name the US states where coal makes up the largest share of in-state electricity generation.

source.name: US Energy Information Administration — State Electricity Profiles

disclaimer: Share of total electricity generated within the state that comes from coal-fired power plants; excludes imported power. Includes Washington DC.
trivia: West Virginia generates about nine-tenths of its electricity from coal — a higher share than any state, though its total output is a fraction of coal-heavy Texas.

title: Highest Natural Gas Share of Electricity
prompt: Name the US states where natural gas makes up the largest share of in-state electricity generation.

source.name: US Energy Information Administration — State Electricity Profiles

disclaimer: Share of in-state electricity generation from natural gas; excludes imports and behind-the-meter generation. Includes Washington DC.

title: Highest Hydropower Share of Electricity
prompt: Name the US states where conventional hydroelectric power supplies the largest share of in-state electricity generation.

source.name: US Energy Information Administration — State Electricity Profiles

disclaimer: Conventional hydroelectric only; excludes pumped-storage hydro (which is net-consumer of electricity). DC not included (source omits it).
trivia: Washington's Grand Coulee Dam alone is the largest hydro plant in the United States, and hydropower supplies roughly two-thirds of the state's electricity.

title: Highest Nuclear Share of Electricity
prompt: Name the US states where nuclear power supplies the largest share of in-state electricity generation.

source.name: US Energy Information Administration — State Electricity Profiles

disclaimer: Share of net in-state generation from nuclear power reactors. DC not included (source omits it).

title: Most Total Electricity Generated
prompt: Name the US states that generate the most total electricity annually across all sources.

source.name: US Energy Information Administration — State Electricity Profiles

disclaimer: Total net electricity generation from all fuels (utility-scale + small-scale) measured in terawatt-hours (TWh). Includes Washington DC.
trivia: Texas generates more electricity than any other state — nearly twice California's output and about one-eighth of the entire US grid.

title: Most Superfund NPL Sites
prompt: Name the US states with the most Superfund sites listed on the EPA National Priorities List, from most to fewest.

source.name: US EPA — Superfund National Priorities List

disclaimer: Counts current and proposed final NPL sites; excludes deleted sites and federal facilities may be listed separately by some tallies. Includes Washington DC.
trivia: New Jersey has the most Superfund NPL sites of any state — a legacy of dense industrial activity and Cold War chemical manufacturing.

title: Most Wind Turbines
prompt: Name the US states with the most utility-scale wind turbines installed.

source.name: USGS — US Wind Turbine Database

disclaimer: Counts operating utility-scale (>=100 kW) turbines only; excludes small distributed and residential turbines. DC not included (source omits it).
trivia: Texas has more wind turbines than the next two states combined, and generates more wind power than any other state.

title: Most Electric Vehicle Registrations
prompt: Name the US states with the most registered plug-in electric vehicles (BEVs).

source.name: US DOE Alternative Fuels Data Center — EV Registrations by State

disclaimer: Counts light-duty battery-electric vehicles registered in the state; excludes plug-in hybrids in some tallies. Includes Washington DC.
trivia: California alone accounts for roughly 37% of all registered electric vehicles in the United States.

title: Most High-Hazard Potential Dams
prompt: Name the US states with the most dams classified as high-hazard-potential by the National Inventory of Dams.

source.name: USACE — National Inventory of Dams

disclaimer: 'High-hazard-potential' means failure would likely cause loss of life; it is not a measure of a dam's current condition. Includes Washington DC.

title: Most Federally Listed Endangered Species
prompt: Name the US states with the most federally listed endangered species under the Endangered Species Act.

source.name: US Fish & Wildlife Service — ECOS Species by State

disclaimer: Counts species federally listed as endangered whose current range includes the state; a species can be counted in multiple states. Includes Washington DC.
trivia: Hawaii — 0.2% of the US land area — hosts more endangered species than any other state, most of them found nowhere else on Earth.

title: Most Toxic Release Inventory Pounds
prompt: Name the US states with the most total on-site and off-site toxic chemical releases reported to the EPA Toxics Release Inventory.

source.name: US EPA — Toxics Release Inventory (TRI) National Analysis

disclaimer: TRI-reported releases include air, water, land, and off-site transfers; a small number of large mining sites can dominate a state's total. Includes Washington DC.
trivia: Alaska tops the TRI list almost entirely because of the Red Dog zinc mine — one facility that reports more toxic releases than most entire states.

title: Most Battery Storage Capacity
prompt: Name the US states with the largest utility-scale battery storage power capacity installed.

source.name: US Energy Information Administration — Preliminary Monthly Electric Generator Inventory

disclaimer: Utility-scale (>=1 MW) battery storage nameplate power capacity, measured in megawatts (MW); excludes behind-the-meter residential and commercial batteries. Includes Washington DC.
trivia: California and Texas together host more grid battery storage than the rest of the country combined, and California alone has more than any country besides China.

title: Most Wildfire Acres Burned Annually
prompt: Name the US states with the most acres burned by wildfires per year, based on a recent multi-year average.

source.name: National Interagency Fire Center — Annual Wildland Fire Statistics

disclaimer: Annual acres burned averaged across 2013-2022; includes both natural and human-caused wildfires but excludes prescribed burns. Includes Washington DC.
trivia: California averages more wildfire acres burned per year than the next two states combined — a mix of fuel loads, drought and extreme fire seasons since 2017.

title: Most Groundwater Withdrawals
prompt: Name the US states that withdraw the most fresh groundwater each day for all uses combined.

source.name: USGS — Estimated Use of Water in the United States

disclaimer: Total fresh groundwater withdrawals across all use categories (irrigation, public supply, industrial, thermoelectric), in millions of gallons per day. Includes Washington DC.
trivia: About three-quarters of the water withdrawn from the High Plains (Ogallala) aquifer goes to irrigate crops in just five states, including Nebraska, Kansas and Texas.

title: Highest Cotton Production
prompt: Name the US states that produce the most upland cotton by bales.

source.name: USDA NASS — Cotton Production by State

disclaimer: Upland cotton, measured in 480-lb bales. DC not included (source omits it).
trivia: Texas typically produces roughly 40% of all US cotton, largely from the High Plains region around Lubbock.

title: Highest Rice Production
prompt: Name the US states that produce the most rice by hundredweight.

source.name: USDA NASS — Rice Stocks / Production

disclaimer: Long-, medium-, and short-grain rice combined; measured in hundredweight (cwt). DC not included (source omits it).
trivia: Arkansas alone accounts for roughly half of all US rice, most of it grown in the Grand Prairie region.

title: Highest Peanut Production
